body: Across 27 Indian winner windows, 17 began at trailing P/E ≤15 (Bajaj Finance 9, Astral 8, Eicher 13, Balkrishna ~2, APL Apollo 5, Deepak 8.5, Tata Elxsi 5, KPIT 8.5, Cochin 5.5, Mazagon 7, HAL 6, Avanti 13, Caplin 12.5, BSE 14, Garware 5, Alkyl 8, BEL 13); their median price multiple was ~266x. Three began at ≥35x (Dixon 40, Kaynes 104, Trent 155, where Trent's EPS was COVID-depressed); their median was ~19x. Two boom-time IPOs at 84x and 214x (Waaree, Premier) tripled EPS and still trade below their first close. Most low-P/E starts were not obscure: they were well-known companies in a panic (Mar 2009, Mar 2020) or companies misclassified as commodity businesses (Balkrishna, APL Apollo, Garware, Avanti). Practical rule for screening: the twin engine needs a low starting multiple. A great business bought at 100x+ has spent the multiple engine, and its return is capped at EPS growth minus de-rating. Caveat: survivorship bias. These are winners picked with hindsight, and many low-P/E stocks stayed cheap or failed (see case_study:suzlon, case_study:capital-goods-2007).
title: Starting P/E ≤15 → median ~266x; starting P/E ≥35 → median ~19x

body: RULE: negative FCF is benign when CFO is positive and the capex earns high returns on proven demand (DMart's owned stores, Bharti's network, APL Apollo's DFT lines), when it funds a durable asset that scales (Netflix content 2018-19: FCF -$3.0 bn and -$3.27 bn, positive from 2020), or when negative CFO reflects a lender's loan growth (Bajaj Finance: negative every year FY15-26 while ROE stayed ~20%). Low CFO/PAT is benign when the working capital is liquid and the business's own (Titan: CFO/PAT 0.62 over FY15-26 because of gold inventory in its stores, funded by gold loans, debtor days 4-8) or when the debtor is sovereign and the delay is budgetary (HAL FY17-19). IT IS SUSPECT WHEN: (1) CFO is weak while receivables or 'loans and advances' grow faster than sales (PC Jeweller exports, Ricoh unbilled revenue, Cox & Kings); (2) the working-capital sign contradicts the business model (a travel company or retailer should be negative); (3) 'capex' goes to related parties or CWIP ages without commissioning; (4) CFO is propped by factoring or customer funds (GE, Wirecard). WARNING: the CFO/PAT test can pass in a trap (Vakrangee FY17-18 CFO > PAT), so it is necessary, not sufficient. TEST: split the cash gap into capex (growth vs maintenance), inventory, receivables (by counterparty), and loans; name the asset created; check incremental ROCE on capex completed 2-3 years ago.

data.benign_if: positive CFO + high-return capex; durable scaling asset; lender loan growth; liquid own inventory; sovereign debtor
data.suspect_if: receivables/advances outgrow sales; WC sign contradicts model; related-party capex; aging CWIP; factoring

title: Reading negative FCF / low CFO: what the cash went into decides
